characters.description: A familiar bonded to Ellie. By borrowing Storm’s power, Ellie can form steel-feathered wings, channel lightning through them, and fly.
characters.name: Storm

characters.description: A huge three-armed creature encountered in an insect-infested ruined town in the Forbidden Lands. It is besieging the town's tower when John directs Ferdie to confront it.
characters.name: three-armed beast

characters.description: A human-shaped legendary captive kept in Soaring Cloud Tower's menagerie from its earliest days. It detects a royal quality in John's scent and says the beasts' king is assembling forces to dominate humankind.
characters.name: captive humanoid legendary beast

characters.description: A giant stone worm assigned to guard a hidden portal for the approaching Beast King. It initially mistakes John for a dragon and reveals that the portal is one part of a larger invasion network intended to bring the beasts into this land.
characters.name: stone-worm portal guard

aliases: dragon soul in John's mana pool
characters.description: A sleeping dragon soul bound to the blue life flame within John's mana pool. It grows stronger as John does and may eventually awaken, seize his body, and turn his increasing power into a threat to the world.
characters.name: dormant dragon spirit

characters.description: The Flying Eagle who commands a wheat shipment from the plains and returns to Sutton Farm with the harvest.
characters.name: Flying Eagle leader

characters.description: Allera's ruler, who now uses the title Iron Monarch and has begun a major offensive against Lepiera. The invading army is heavily armored and equipped with lightning weapons.
characters.name: Iron Monarch

characters.description: The leader of the Holy Knights, arriving at Sutton Farm to ask the Eternal Flame for aid. High Marshal Helbright reports that Lepiera's army is collapsing before tireless armored troops and remains to await John's answer.
characters.name: High Marshal Helbright

characters.description: One of the robed figures Ben discovers inside a sealed guardroom above Lepiera's capital gate as the invading army approaches.
characters.name: hostile gate mage

characters.description: The officer carrying the Ecclesia banner during the defense of Lepiera's capital. Despite being wounded at the broken main gate, the commander stays with the Holy Knights during their counterattack.
characters.name: capital city commander

characters.description: One of Ben's two small specter guardians. Aurora emerges from the shadows beside Henluin when Ben joins the defense of the breached capital gate, attacking threats with exceptional speed and protecting him amid the invading soldiers.
characters.name: Aurora

characters.description: One of the two small specters assigned to protect Ben. Henluin fights alongside Aurora at the shattered gate, intervening when Ben and the wounded defenders face the invading force and helping keep his young charge alive.
characters.name: Henluin

characters.description: A curse-bound mage organization supporting the invasion of Lepiera's capital. Its representatives demand surrender and claim they intend to replace a failed world order, but they cannot disclose the identity of their master.
characters.name: Order of the New Dawn

characters.description: The senior leader of the plains alliance. John appoints the supreme khan to the Ecclesia council and gives the leader command of the independent Swift Wind Army.
characters.name: supreme khan

characters.description: A returning guardian of the Old Way and an ally from John's earlier struggles. Togine remains away from the central events of this volume until Katrine's final warning confirms his death.
characters.name: Togine

characters.description: An interstellar raiding organization that exploits less powerful worlds for resources and captives. The Cabal has learned the location of John's world and is coming, making it an immediate apocalypse-level danger.
characters.name: Cabal of the Broken Gate

recaps.ending: Lepiera's capital survives both attacks. Ferdie and Sigvald destroy the second Iron Monarch body, while the legendary beasts rout the duplicate army. John takes ten Order of the New Dawn mages alive, although two senior mages escape toward the production base. High Marshal Helbright arrives with the plains forces and receives orders to restore the border, clear remaining invaders, and manage the movement of civilians from occupied Allera settlements. John, Ellie, Ferdie, and the captives return to Shadow Tower. The prisoners carry three linked curses involving coerced loyalty, fate, and stolen life, leaving the Order's master and its possible connection to Soaring Cloud Tower unresolved. John resumes farm expansion, but the dragon spirit remains inside him and three beast portals are still active. Katrine then sends a desperate message from beyond the world: Togine is dead, she disclosed the world's location under torture, and the Cabal of the Broken Gate is coming to exploit and enslave it.
recaps.in_short: John Sutton expands Sutton Farm's mana-cleansing wheat into mills, noodles, and portable meals while investigating several linked threats. A visit to Soaring Cloud Tower exposes slavery, loyalty conditioning, and a prophecy of a Beast Tide. John destroys one of four beast portals, then learns that his blue flame contains a dragon spirit that wants his body. When the Iron Monarch's duplicate army invades Lepiera, Ellie helps John resist the dragon's influence and return as the Eternal Flame. Ben uncovers sabotage at the capital gate, John saves the first defense, and Ferdie leads legendary beasts that break the second assault. Ten enemy mages are captured, but their leaders and production base remain free. As John returns to farm and tower work, Katrine warns that Togine is dead and the Cabal of the Broken Gate has learned the world's location, creating an imminent interstellar threat.

recaps.text: Previously: John Sutton established Sutton Farm in a mana-damaged valley and became a public leader through the Ecclesia, although he now wants a life centered on farming rather than war. Ellie remains his closest partner, combining witchcraft, invention, and practical judgment. Ben is growing into a trained classholder under the protection of the household and two hidden specters. Ferdie and Sigvald are powerful animal companions who defend the farm. John's work has become larger than the farm itself: his wheat can consume harmful mana, while a reverse-filter enchantment helps prevent dangerously pure mana from destabilizing the world. Former allies and rulers have gathered around the valley, and Shadow Tower preserves research connected to the First Mage. John also carries blue dragon flame and immense power, but the full consequences of that inheritance are not yet understood. Beyond the valley, Allera is unstable, Lepiera faces growing pressure, and food shortages threaten ordinary people.

So far this book: John finds that his experimental wheat has not yet removed the valley's remaining mana taint, while a mysterious counter assigns him ten apocalypse points. Refugees fleeing hunger and the expected Allera-Lepiera war pour into Fairford, where John approves settlement for those willing to work. He also helps researchers calculate an activation for the First Mage's doorway. A hostile hermit opens it early to an unknown world, attacks the group with unusually dense golden mana, and is apparently killed after his summoned dragon drags him through. The incident proves that powers beyond this world can make contact. John continues the harvest and improves a mechanical combine while war and food prices worsen. Ben asks to leave the valley for a merchant apprenticeship, forcing John and Ellie to weigh safety against his independence. Ellie recognizes that Ben needs greater independence, but her final consent is still pending. With a properly calculated destination ready, Katrine and an elder sage pass through the doorway, planning to return after a year.

John's promise to remain in this world until it is restored reduces his apocalypse count from ten to nine, though the system gives no explanation. Ben departs with the merchant, and John turns the harvest toward famine relief. With help from the Shadow Tower plant administrator, he separates wheat into refined flour and begins designing a mana-powered mill. Ellie tests bread and solves the noodle recipe, while Rebea helps construct machinery and manage excess mana. The farm expands rapidly, adding workers, cattle, and large-scale baking capacity. The work is interrupted when raiders burn Jem and chain its residents. John, Ellie, Thomas, Ferdie, and Sigvald rescue the settlement, defeat the attackers, and accept their surrender. Eva places a lethal brand on the prisoners for control. Jem is safe, but the captured force's sponsor and purpose have not yet been established, leaving John with both an urgent investigation and a growing food operation.

The Jem prisoners reveal that a count ordered the raid and that two captive mages came from Soaring Cloud Tower. Koeri identifies its three masters as Joro, Orateth, and the Forgelord. John and Ellie travel toward the tower with the mages and Ferdie, learning that the tower accepts human thralls and predicts a world-ending Beast Tide. Koeri's missing childhood memories, altered age, and cursed bracer suggest that the tower also conditions its own disciples. Before reaching it, the party stops in the Forbidden Lands, where enchanted insects threaten a crucial wheat harvest. John confirms that the crop is safe, then leads an assault on the swarm's nest. His immense flood spell destroys most of the ruined town above it but creates a corrosive mana storm, forcing the group underground. They fight to a chamber containing a device that manufactures insects from a specimen trapped in amber. John removes the specimen, damages the machine, and drains the storm, ending the immediate infestation. Recent replacement parts show that someone had deliberately kept the ancient device operating.

John heals the great beast Ferdie fought, then enters Soaring Cloud Tower through a vast sensory curse. Inside, laborers who failed mage training live as collared thralls. Orateth explains that the tower hid for more than two centuries after a prophecy warned of humanity's enslavement by beasts. She says its masters now want to unite humanity, but Ellie discovers that the guests' food and tea contain an accumulating loyalty drug. A captive legendary beast confirms that a Beast King is raising armies, and John's quest identifies the Beast Tide as the first of three major apocalypse threats. When the masters test him, John withstands the Forgelord's attack and reveals his mana-less blue flame. Their attitude changes immediately. John trades a sample of that flame for shared research and secures a non-aggression agreement, but refuses an offer to become a fourth master. Ellie objects that the arrangement leaves the tower's slavery intact. On their departure, they discover that an unknown party has already excavated the disabled insect machine.

Back at Sutton Farm, John commits the Ecclesia to an explicit anti-slavery position while the missing insect machine remains a future danger. Shadow Tower research connects its duplication spell to ancient theories that cannot copy minds or souls, leaving the living insects unexplained. John also tests a dangerous growth treatment. The process, called manamorphosis, strengthens his body and reveals that his blue dragon flame functions as an unusual, extremely dense mana pool, but the treatment is unsafe for anyone else. Reopening the iron mine exposes a vast cavern where a stone worm guards one of four portals prepared for the Beast King's invasion. John destroys that portal and spares the guard under a flame constraint. Records then explain why the underground witnesses fear him: dragon spirits can survive death and manipulate new hosts. John recognizes the archived dragon as the source of his blue flame. A quest confirms that its soul sleeps inside his mana pool, grows whenever he grows stronger, and may eventually take his body. Ellie helps him accept the danger without surrendering his own identity.

A plains caravan delivers wheat, allowing Sutton Farm's automated mills and noodle lines to begin supplying portable meals at scale. Its leader also brings news that Allera's ruler now calls himself the Iron Monarch and has launched a major invasion of Lepiera with armored troops and lightning weapons. High Marshal Helbright arrives to ask John to return to battle, reporting that the enemy kills resisters, enslaves survivors, and overwhelms Lepiera's retreating army. John hesitates because killing increases his power and strengthens his desire to use it. That conflict gives the dragon spirit an opening to attack his mind. Ellie and Sigvald enter the struggle, and Ellie reaches John through their bond and the remembered ideal of the Eternal Flame as hope rather than domination. John forces the dragon back, but now knows it can try to possess him. He agrees to help the threatened population without treating the war as service to a nation. Ellie and Ferdie join him, Thomas remains to defend and supply the farm, and John resumes command of the Eternal Flame.

At Lepiera's capital, Ben persuades his merchant associates to donate their food stores before the siege. He then discovers robed saboteurs preparing to destroy the main gate. Ben disrupts them and warns the city, but a hostile mage still blasts open the gate and lets the Iron Monarch's tireless armored troops into the breach. Ben, Aurora, and Henluin support the defenders until John and Ellie arrive. John kills the fleeing hostile mage, seals the breach with flame, and confronts the Iron Monarch. The emperor's armor absorbs nearby mana and counters direct magic, but John releases more of his internal power, assumes a blue-flame armored form, and physically defeats him. The invading army retreats, buying only a short reprieve. Before interrogation, the Iron Monarch's body destroys itself. Examination of other corpses reveals identical manufactured soldiers whose bodies vanish outside their armor. John and Ellie conclude that an external system creates bodies and installs collected souls within them. The production base and enemy mages remain active, while every death John causes risks strengthening the dragon's influence.

John rewards Aurora and Henluin for protecting Ben and promises both specters another favor. With no quarry close enough, he orders part of the palace dismantled so citizens can rebuild the gate and walls before the enemy returns. His appeal to place lives above symbols spreads the Eternal Flame's blessing among the workers. The next duplicate army is far larger. Four mages from the Order of the New Dawn demand surrender and claim to seek a new order for humanity, but a curse prevents them from identifying their master. John releases them with an ultimatum, and the attack begins under a replacement Iron Monarch. Enemy mages keep John occupied while he tries to capture rather than kill them, limiting the dragon spirit's leverage. Ben and the city commander delay the duplicate emperor until Ferdie arrives as a legendary draconic bull leading other legendary beasts. Ferdie and Sigvald destroy the emperor's armor and kill the duplicate. The beasts rout the army, John captures the enemy mages, and two powerful enemies escape toward their base.

High Marshal Helbright and the allied plains forces reach the liberated capital after the battle. John orders them to clear the remaining invaders, restore the border, secure populated Allera settlements, and move civilians into Lepiera. He then returns with Ellie, Ferdie, and ten captured Order mages to Shadow Tower. Ellie finds that Ferdie's purified mana offers protection from divination and fate magic. She also detects a coercive plant extract in the prisoners, raising a possible connection to the conditioning used at Soaring Cloud Tower. The plant administrator identifies three curses on the captives: enforced obedience linked to the drug, fate-binding, and theft of life that accelerates aging. The Order's master, production system, escaped leaders, and relationship to the tower remain unresolved. John resumes plans for winter wheat and a larger farm, while the dragon spirit and three beast portals remain active dangers. Katrine then sends a final warning: Togine is dead, she revealed the world's location under torture, and the Cabal of the Broken Gate is pursuing her and coming to exploit and enslave the world.

characters.description: A Greek god who argues that animals would be even more miserable than humans if given human intelligence. He accepts a wager with Hermes and grants consciousness to the dogs staying overnight at a Toronto veterinary clinic.
characters.name: Apollo

characters.description: The Greek god who disputes Apollo's bleak judgment of mortals. He wagers that if dogs receive human intelligence, at least one will die happy, and he follows the animals' lives with sympathy while remaining bound by the terms of the bet.
characters.name: Hermes

characters.description: A powerful mastiff who emerges as the leader of the escaped dogs. He values the inherited order of canine life and sees the new capacity for abstract thought as a threat to the pack's unity and to his authority.
characters.name: Atticus

characters.description: A black poodle among the dogs transformed by Apollo and Hermes. Thoughtful and independent, he is less willing than Atticus to suppress the dogs' new intelligence and eventually seeks a way to live in the human city.
characters.name: Majnoun

characters.description: A small, clever dog whose intelligence is joined to a strong instinct for self-preservation. He reads the pack's shifting loyalties quickly and attaches himself to those most likely to protect him.
characters.name: Benjy

characters.description: One of the transformed dogs and the most devoted to the language the pack invents. He delights in sound, pattern, and metaphor, composing poems that preserve a distinctly canine way of sensing the world.
characters.name: Prince

characters.description: A Toronto woman who takes in Majnoun and treats him as a thinking companion rather than a pet. Patient and curious, she builds a shared vocabulary with him and tries to understand the boundaries between human and canine experience.
characters.name: Nira

characters.description: Nira's husband. He is less comfortable than she is with Majnoun's unusual awareness and with the intense bond that develops between the woman and the dog.
characters.name: Miguel

recaps.ending: By the closing stages of the wager, the original pack has been destroyed by violence, age, and the difficulty of reconciling canine instincts with human-style consciousness. Majnoun's years with Nira have given him a relationship based on communication and mutual trust. His life ends with the knowledge that he has been loved, allowing him to die happy and satisfying Hermes's condition. Prince survives far longer than the other dogs. Apollo burdens his final years with isolation, but cannot erase the poet's delight in language. Near death, Prince encounters a human who responds to one of his poems, and that moment of recognition also gives him happiness. Hermes therefore wins the wager. The gods' contest is decided not by comfort or long life, but by the dogs' capacity to create meaning through love, language, and being understood.
recaps.in_short: In a Toronto tavern, Apollo and Hermes wager over whether human intelligence would make animals more miserable. They grant consciousness and language to fifteen dogs in a veterinary clinic, then wait to see whether any will die happy. The escaped animals form a pack, but their gift divides them. Atticus tries to preserve a traditional canine hierarchy and suppresses the new language, while violence and rivalry reduce the group. Majnoun leaves and forms a profound friendship with a woman named Nira; through patience they learn to communicate across the species divide. Prince, the pack's poet, is driven away but continues composing verse. Most of the dogs die frightened, betrayed, or isolated. Majnoun eventually dies secure in Nira's love, fulfilling the wager's condition. Prince lives longest, and despite Apollo's efforts to make his final life bitter, he experiences a last moment in which a human understands his poetry. Hermes wins because consciousness brings suffering but also makes love, art, and recognized meaning possible.

recaps.text: Apollo and Hermes debate human unhappiness in a Toronto tavern. To test whether intelligence itself is a curse, they wager on a group of fifteen dogs spending the night at a nearby veterinary clinic. The gods give the animals human consciousness and the power to develop complex language; Hermes wins if even one dog eventually dies happy. The dogs awaken to unfamiliar ideas about time, mortality, and selfhood, escape the clinic, and gather in High Park. They create words suited to canine senses, but the gift immediately divides them. Atticus establishes himself as leader and favors instinct, hierarchy, and unity. Majnoun, Prince, and others are drawn to thought and invention. As fear and competition grow, the pack begins to punish dogs who embrace the change too openly, turning the gods' experiment into a struggle over what kind of beings they will become.

Atticus consolidates control of the pack by opposing the transformed dogs' elaborate language and by treating humanlike reflection as disloyalty. The group's intelligence does not remove older drives toward dominance, territory, and survival; instead it gives those drives new political forms. Violence scatters the animals who do not fit Atticus's order. Majnoun leaves the pack and is taken in by Nira, who senses that he is no ordinary dog. Rather than demanding obedience, she experiments with sounds and meanings until they can communicate. Their relationship becomes an exchange between two minds with different senses and assumptions. Nira's husband, Miguel, remains uneasy about the place Majnoun occupies in their household, but Nira and Majnoun continue building trust.

The surviving dogs follow sharply different paths. Benjy relies on calculation and shifting loyalties, while the old pack's conflicts consume more of its members. Prince, whose poems transform smell, sound, and canine memory into a new art, is rejected by dogs who fear that language has carried them too far from their nature. He survives outside the pack and keeps composing despite having no audience able to understand him. Majnoun's life with Nira offers another answer to the wager. Their vocabulary remains imperfect, yet each learns to accept what the other cannot fully translate. Majnoun comes to understand companionship as a chosen bond rather than ownership, and Nira treats his differences as part of his personhood. The gods continue watching as happiness remains possible but fragile.

Time, violence, and betrayal eliminate the remnants of Atticus's pack, leaving the wager to be decided by the dogs whose lives moved beyond it. Majnoun grows old after years of friendship with Nira. Their shared language and mutual care allow him to recognize that he has been loved; he dies with that assurance and is happy at the end, meeting Hermes's condition. Prince outlives the other transformed dogs and retains both his poems and his delight in making them. Apollo tries to prevent another happy death by deepening Prince's loneliness, but near the end a human responds to the pattern and meaning of his verse. Prince dies having been understood. Hermes wins the wager: the dogs' intelligence caused division, grief, and fear, but it also enabled love and art to give suffering a meaning that instinct alone could not have supplied.

characters.description: The younger Dragna sister, who came out of the last Caraval having settled her debt and helped set the Fates loose on the empire. She has her mother back and she knows who Legend really is. She is still the sister who acts first and reckons the cost afterward, and she is discovering that everything she was told about the Fates before they walked free was the polite version.
characters.name: Donatella Dragna

characters.description: The elder Dragna sister, who won the first Caraval and has spent the time since trying to build an ordinary life out of a family that never permitted one. She is steadier than Tella and far less willing to gamble, and she carries unfinished business with Julian into a capital that has larger problems than either of them.
characters.name: Scarlett Dragna

characters.description: The master of Caraval, whose real name and face Tella now knows. He is no longer the remote figure Scarlett once wrote letters to: he is a person with a history, designs of his own, and a company of performers who do what he asks without asking why. What passed between him and Tella at the end of the last game was left unresolved.
characters.name: Legend

characters.description: One of the Fates, immortal, and lethal to anyone he kisses except the one person he has spent a very long time failing to find. He got what he wanted out of the last Caraval and remains entirely indifferent to what it cost the people who helped him get it. He has not stopped circling Tella.
characters.name: Jacks

characters.description: One of Legend's performers, and the man Scarlett has never managed to decide about. He has been more honest with her than he used to be, which is not the same as being easy to trust after two games' worth of playing a part.
characters.name: Julian

characters.description: The sisters' mother, recovered at the end of the last book after years of absence. She knows a great deal about the Fates and about how they came to be bound, considerably more than she has explained to her daughters, and she is the one who told them that freeing them was a disaster rather than a triumph.
characters.name: Paloma Dragna

characters.description: The immortals of the old stories, pictured on the Deck of Destiny and imprisoned long ago, now released and moving through the Meridian Empire as people rather than as cards. They are worse than the tales about them suggested, they have quarrels and appetites of their own, and nobody in the empire is equipped to deal with them.
characters.name: The Fates

recaps.text:
In the first book, Scarlett and Donatella Dragna got off the island of Trisda and away from their violent father to attend Caraval, the performance game staged once a year by a showman known only as Legend. Tella was taken as the game's prize, and Scarlett spent five nights buying clues with secrets, memories and days of her life to find her, watching both her sister and a sailor named Julian appear to die before the game closed. All of it was staged: Julian was one of Legend's performers, and Tella had agreed in advance to play the missing prize. Scarlett won. Tella had her own reason for taking the part - she had bargained with a stranger who promised word of Paloma, the mother who abandoned them, in exchange for Legend's true name.

In the second book Tella played the next Caraval, staged in Valenda for Empress Elantine's birthday, to settle that debt. She was shadowed by Jacks, who proved to be the Prince of Hearts: one of the Fates, the immortals pictured on the Deck of Destiny she inherited from her mother, imprisoned long ago and determined to get out. The game's clues ran directly through the history of how the Fates were bound, and Tella was steered into helping free them. Legend's true name was given up and the disguise he ran the game behind was broken - he had been playing the performer Dante, at Tella's side throughout. Empress Elantine died during her own celebrations, telling Donatella first that the Dragna sisters are her family. Paloma was recovered, and her response was not relief but a warning: the Fates walking free is a catastrophe. That is where this book opens - the Fates loose in the empire, the imperial succession unsettled, and both sisters standing in the middle of it.

characters.description: A seventeen-year-old orphan raised among thieves in Lant Street, London. She is loyal to the household that has protected her and understands pickpocketing and fraud as ordinary trades. When Gentleman proposes that she pose as a lady's maid in a confidence scheme, she accepts in the hope of earning a share of the fortune.
characters.name: Susan Trinder

characters.description: The woman who raised Sue in her Lant Street home after the death of Sue's mother. She cares for unwanted infants for payment and presides over a close household of thieves. To Sue she is a loving foster mother whose approval carries great weight.
characters.name: Mrs Sucksby

characters.description: A polished confidence man who visits Lant Street with an elaborate plan. He intends to court the wealthy Maud Lilly under an assumed identity, marry her, gain control of her money, and have her confined as insane. He recruits Sue to become Maud's maid and guide the deception from inside the country house.
characters.name: Richard Rivers

characters.description: Mrs Sucksby's partner in the Lant Street household. He runs a locksmith's shop as a front and works with stolen goods, providing a calm, practical counterweight to the busier life around him.
characters.name: Mr Ibbs

characters.description: A young thief and member of the Lant Street household. She grew up alongside Sue and helps prepare her for the unfamiliar work and clothing of a lady's maid.
characters.name: Dainty

characters.description: A volatile boy in the Lant Street household who participates in its criminal work. He often quarrels with Sue and Dainty and treats the proposed fraud as another opportunity for profit.
characters.name: John Vroom

characters.description: A wealthy young woman living in isolation at Briar with her uncle. Orphaned as a child and trained to serve as his secretary, she appears sheltered, nervous, and inexperienced. Sue is placed beside her as a maid so that Gentleman can gain her confidence and persuade her to marry him.
characters.name: Maud Lilly

characters.description: Maud's reclusive uncle and guardian at Briar. A scholar and collector, he has trained Maud as his secretary and keeps the household ordered around his library work. His strict routines leave her with little contact with the wider world.
characters.name: Mr Lilly

characters.description: A servant boy at Briar who becomes devoted to Gentleman. His access to the grounds and his willingness to help make him useful when plans at the house begin to unravel.
characters.name: Charles

characters.description: A senior woman in the Briar household who remembers Maud's arrival and oversees the female servants. Her severe manner and loyalty to Mr Lilly reinforce the controlled atmosphere in which Maud lives.
characters.name: Mrs Stiles

characters.description: A physician who receives the woman Gentleman identifies as his unstable wife. He interprets resistance as proof of illness and uses the authority of the asylum to strip her of her name, freedom, and credibility.
characters.name: Dr Christie

characters.description: The Lilly woman whose hidden arrangements connect Sue, Maud, Mrs Sucksby, and the disputed inheritance. Her written account reveals that Sue is her daughter and explains the exchange of the two babies after their births.
characters.name: Marianne Lilly

recaps.ending: Sue escapes the asylum and returns to Lant Street, where she discovers Maud living under Mrs Sucksby's control. The confrontation exposes a scheme older than Gentleman's fraud: as infants, Sue and Maud were exchanged. Sue is Marianne Lilly's daughter and the true Lilly heir, while Maud is Mrs Sucksby's biological daughter. Gentleman dies during the struggle. Mrs Sucksby accepts responsibility for the killing and is hanged, protecting Maud while leaving Sue Marianne's written explanation. Sue initially believes Maud knowingly stole her entire life and separates from her. When Sue later returns to Briar, she finds that Maud has survived by writing erotic material for sale. Their conversation establishes that both were manipulated and betrayed, even though each also betrayed the other under pressure. They acknowledge their love and reunite at Briar. The inheritance plot is resolved, Gentleman and Mrs Sucksby are dead, and Sue and Maud end the novel together with a chance to build a life outside the identities others imposed on them.
recaps.in_short: Susan Trinder, raised in a London thieves' household, agrees to become maid to the wealthy Maud Lilly as part of Gentleman's plan to marry Maud, seize her fortune, and confine her. Sue and Maud fall in love, but after the marriage Sue is committed in Maud's place. Maud's narration reveals that she knew the scheme and had been promised escape from her uncle's oppressive home, though Gentleman then delivers her to Mrs Sucksby. Sue escapes the asylum and returns to Lant Street. There she learns that she and Maud were exchanged as babies: Sue is the Lilly heir, while Maud is Mrs Sucksby's daughter. Gentleman dies in the ensuing struggle, and Mrs Sucksby is executed after taking responsibility. Sue eventually finds Maud back at Briar, supporting herself by writing erotic fiction. Recognizing how both were used, the two women reconcile and remain together.

recaps.text: Susan Trinder has grown up in a thieves' household in Lant Street under the care of Mrs Sucksby and Mr Ibbs. A confidence man called Gentleman proposes a profitable deception. Maud Lilly, an orphaned heiress, lives at the isolated country house Briar with her scholarly uncle. Gentleman has entered the household under another name and plans to make Maud fall in love with him. Once married, he can have her declared insane and take control of her fortune. Sue is to pose as an experienced lady's maid, encourage the courtship, and help manage Maud; in return, she will receive a large payment. At Briar, Sue finds Maud timid and closely governed by her uncle's routines. As Sue learns the duties she only pretended to know, Maud begins to rely on her. Gentleman presses his courtship while Sue tries to treat the vulnerable young woman as merely the object of a fraud.

Sue becomes Maud's confidante and helps Gentleman create opportunities for a secret courtship. The closeness between the two women develops into mutual desire, making Sue increasingly ashamed of the plan, but loyalty to Mrs Sucksby and fear of Gentleman's reaction keep her from confessing. Maud agrees to flee Briar and marry Gentleman. After the private wedding, the three travel toward London and stop at a mental asylum, supposedly to arrange Maud's confinement. There the deception reverses: Maud and Gentleman identify Sue as the delusional wife, using Sue's own history and behavior to support their story. The doctors accept their account and imprison Sue under Maud's name. Maud leaves with Gentleman, while Sue realizes that the woman she meant to betray has anticipated and redirected the entire scheme against her.

The story returns to Maud's childhood. She spends her first years in a harsh institution before her uncle takes her to Briar. He trains her to read aloud and assist with his private collection of explicit books, presenting her to male collectors while keeping her ignorant of ordinary life. Maud learns to hide disgust and anger behind obedience. Mrs Stiles enforces the household's rules, and the library becomes both Maud's work and the instrument of her confinement. By the time Gentleman arrives, Maud understands that her inheritance will not necessarily free her from her uncle's control. His offer of escape therefore reaches someone who is sheltered but not innocent, practiced in performance, and desperate to choose what happens to her own life.

From Maud's perspective, Gentleman offers a scheme in which Sue will be confined and Maud will escape Briar with a share of her fortune. Maud recognizes Sue as an accomplice but still becomes emotionally and sexually attached to her. She considers abandoning the plot, yet years of coercion and Gentleman's pressure lead her through the marriage and the substitution at the asylum. Her apparent calm during Sue's commitment conceals the cost of the betrayal. Gentleman then takes Maud to Lant Street rather than granting the independence he promised. Mrs Sucksby receives her with unsettling familiarity and helps keep her confined. Maud discovers that Gentleman and Mrs Sucksby have additional plans for her money and that the Lant Street household is connected to her past in ways she was never told. Both women are now trapped under each other's identities: Sue in the asylum as Maud, and Maud among the people Sue believed were her family.

Sue refuses the identity forced on her at the asylum, but her insistence that she is Susan Trinder is treated as evidence of madness. She learns enough about the institution's routines to seize an opportunity to escape. With help connected to Charles, the servant boy from Briar, she makes her way back toward London, determined to confront Maud and Gentleman. At Lant Street, Maud remains under Mrs Sucksby's control while the adults wait for the financial arrangement attached to her supposed identity to mature. She begins to understand that the fraud at Briar was only one layer of a longer plan. Sue's return brings the two halves of the story together, but each still believes the other knowingly chose the betrayal that ruined her life.

Sue reaches Lant Street and confronts Maud, Gentleman, and Mrs Sucksby. The struggle exposes the older secret behind the inheritance: Sue is the daughter of Marianne Lilly and the rightful heir, while Maud is Mrs Sucksby's biological daughter. The babies were exchanged, placing Maud in the Lilly family and Sue in Lant Street, and the later fraud was designed around that hidden substitution. Gentleman is fatally stabbed during the confrontation. Mrs Sucksby claims responsibility and is executed, protecting Maud and leaving Sue access to Marianne's written explanation. Sue initially separates from Maud, convinced that too much betrayal lies between them. Eventually she returns to Briar and finds Maud there, earning money by writing erotic fiction. Their meeting clarifies that each loved the other and that both were manipulated by Gentleman and Mrs Sucksby, even while making damaging choices of their own. Sue and Maud reconcile and remain together at Briar, no longer living inside the roles others designed for them.

characters.description: Seventeen years old and the last human monster in the Dells: a young woman whose hair runs through every shade of red, gold and orange, whose beauty pulls at everyone who sees her, and who can enter minds, read them and steer them. She lives quietly in the far north of the kingdom, keeping her hair covered, hunted by monster predators drawn to her blood and by people who loved or hated her father. She is a serious musician, teaches the local children, and refuses to use her power on anyone if she can avoid it, because she saw exactly what such a power does in the hands of someone who enjoys it.
characters.name: Fire

characters.description: Lord Brocker's son, Fire's oldest friend and her sometime lover, an archer of such accuracy that his name has become a joke about him. He is generous and quick, and also jealous, possessive of Fire and unable to stop himself pursuing other women, which is the running argument of their lives.
characters.name: Archer

characters.description: Archer's father, lord of a northern holding and once the commander of the King's Army, considered the finest military mind the Dells has produced. King Nax had his legs broken years ago and he has used a wheeled chair ever since. He raised Fire alongside his own son, and he still advises the crown's soldiers when they come north.
characters.name: Lord Brocker

characters.description: Fire's father, dead before the book begins. He was a human monster of extraordinary power who took hold of King Nax's mind and, through him, of the kingdom, ruling by whim and cruelty for decades and leaving the Dells lawless and near bankrupt when he died. He adored his daughter, which is the part Fire finds hardest, and everything she fears about herself she learned by watching him.
characters.name: Cansrel

characters.description: Commander of the King's Army and brother to the king, a hard, plain-spoken man who has spent his adult life holding the kingdom together with soldiers because its government cannot. He hates monsters and distrusts Fire on sight, for reasons that go back to what Cansrel did to his father and to the Dells.
characters.name: Prince Brigan

characters.description: King Nax's widow, who keeps her own fortified holding in the north and a great deal of the kingdom's remaining common sense. She is a shrewd political operator, one of the few people who treats Fire as an asset rather than a temptation or a threat, and she knows more about the last reign than she says.
characters.name: Queen Roen

characters.description: King of the Dells, Nax's eldest son, a decent man trying to rule a kingdom his father ruined and largely failing. He is honest about his own weakness in front of Fire, whose power over minds he can barely withstand.
characters.name: King Nash

characters.description: Nax's daughter, half-sister to Nash and Brigan, who runs the crown's intelligence work with her brother Garan. Sharp, unsentimental and openly curious about what Fire's power could do for them.
characters.name: Princess Clara

characters.description: Nax's son, half-brother to Nash and Brigan, who manages the crown's spies and its accounts alongside Clara. He is chronically ill and works through it, and he is slower than his sister to trust a monster in the palace.
characters.name: Prince Garan

characters.description: Brigan's small daughter, about five years old, raised in the palace by her aunts and uncles. She is fearless, horse-mad, and entirely unbothered by monsters, and she attaches herself to Fire immediately.
characters.name: Hanna

characters.description: The soldier who commands Fire's personal guard, chosen because her mind holds firm against a monster's pull. Steady, direct, and unwilling to let her charge out of sight.
characters.name: Musa

characters.description: One of the young soldiers assigned to Fire's guard, quiet and competent, who has her own reasons for being uncomfortable around Archer.
characters.name: Mila

characters.description: A great lord of the north with lands on the Pikkian border, who has spent years building a private army larger than the crown can comfortably ignore. He is courteous to the king and openly contemptuous of the king's authority.
characters.name: Lord Mydogg

characters.description: A great lord of the south, the crown's other looming problem, wealthy, vain, and gathering his own force for a move on the throne. He is less capable than his northern rival and more easily flattered.
characters.name: Lord Gentian

characters.description: Mydogg's sister, married into the Pikkian nobility and at least as dangerous as her brother. She is the one holding his alliances together and she does not underestimate Fire.
characters.name: Murgda

characters.description: A boy with strangely mismatched eyes, found in the far north, whose father came into the Dells from the unknown country beyond the western mountains. Whatever he says, people do: his power is in his words, it leaves minds foggy and obedient afterwards, and it is the explanation for the blank-minded men who have been turning up all through the kingdom. He is curious, patient and entirely without pity.
characters.name: The boy

recaps.ending: The rebellion is fought out in two campaigns and broken. Fire, who has spent the book refusing to be what her father was, ends up using her power at the scale he used his - reaching across a battlefield into thousands of minds - and chooses to use it to stop killing rather than to command. She survives; so do Nash and Brigan; the great lords' rising fails. Archer is dead, and the woman carrying his child, one of Fire's own guards, has the support of Fire and of Brocker's household. Brigan is revealed to be Brocker's son rather than King Nax's, which is why Nax crippled Brocker years ago, and which makes Brigan and Archer half-brothers - a truth that arrives too late for either of them to do anything with. Fire takes a place at the centre of the kingdom rather than hiding at its edge, working for the crown and for Brigan, whom she loves and will not marry into a throne for. She also settles the question of her bloodline deliberately: there will be no more human monsters after her. The boy with the fogging voice is not caught. He goes west, back through the mountains his father came out of, into the country nobody in the Dells knows anything about, which is where the story of the seven kingdoms begins.
recaps.in_short: In the Dells, a land of brilliantly coloured 'monster' creatures that captivate the minds of anyone who looks at them, seventeen-year-old Fire is the last human monster: irresistible to look at and able to enter and control minds. Her father Cansrel used the same gift to own King Nax and wreck the kingdom, and Fire has spent her life refusing to become him. With the Dells sliding toward civil war between two rebel lords, the crown asks her to use her power on prisoners and spies. She agrees, moves to King's City, and works with King Nash, his army commander Brigan, and their half-siblings Clara and Garan, gradually falling in love with Brigan. A second mind-worker is at large: a boy from beyond the western mountains whose words compel obedience. He kills Fire's oldest friend Archer and takes her prisoner in the north during the war. Fire escapes, the rebellion is defeated, and she uses her power across a battlefield to stop the fighting rather than direct it. She stays in the Dells as the crown's ally, and decides the monster line ends with her; the boy escapes westward.

recaps.text: This book stands on its own. It is set in the Dells, a country entirely separate from the seven kingdoms of Graceling, on the other side of an impassable mountain range, and none of its people have ever heard of Graces or of the kingdoms to the west. Readers coming from Graceling should know only that the two books share one thread: the origin of a person from that western country whose power works on the mind through his words, and how he came to cross the mountains. Everything else here - the monsters, the Dellian royal family, the war for the throne - is new, and the Dells' own history is all the background required.

In the Dells, monsters are ordinary creatures born in impossible colours - raptors, insects, big cats, and very rarely people - whose beauty seizes the minds of anyone who looks at them and whose flesh draws other monsters to feed. Fire, seventeen, is the last human monster: hair in every shade of red and gold, a face nobody can look away from, and the ability to read and move through minds. She lives in the far north near Lord Brocker and his son Archer, her lifelong friend and lover. Her father Cansrel was a monster too, and used his power to own King Nax's mind and run the kingdom into ruin through decades of cruelty and waste; Fire is terrified of the same appetite in herself, and holds back from using her power at all. Near her home a poacher shoots her, and when he is killed and Fire examines what is left of him, she finds his mind was strangely fogged and blank - not confusion, but something done to him. Nobody can say who he was or what emptied him out.

The kingdom Cansrel left behind is close to collapse. King Nash rules a country with no working government, kept upright only by his brother Prince Brigan and the King's Army, which spends its time putting down banditry and warlords. Two great lords, Mydogg in the north and Gentian in the south, are quietly assembling armies for a move on the throne. Brigan comes north and makes no secret of despising monsters and distrusting Cansrel's daughter. Queen Roen, Nax's widow, and Brocker both see Fire differently: her power to read minds is the one advantage the crown has, and the crown is asking for it. Fire is invited to King's City to question prisoners and captured spies. She refuses, because using her power on an unwilling mind is precisely what her father did, then changes her mind, and travels south under guard with the army.

At the palace Fire meets the rest of the royal family: Nash, who is honest about barely being able to withstand her; Clara and Garan, Nax's other children, who run the crown's intelligence; and Brigan's small daughter Hanna, who takes to her at once. Fire agrees to sit in on interrogations, and hates the work even as it proves decisive - she can tell who is lying, and she can take what a prisoner will not give. Some of the captured minds are fogged in exactly the way the poacher's was, which means a second person with power over minds is operating somewhere in the Dells, and using it on the rebels' behalf or on their enemies. Fire's memories of her father fill in around this: how Cansrel took hold of King Nax, what he did to people for amusement, how he loved his daughter and expected her to become what he was, and how she spent her childhood learning to hold her own power back from the uses he had in mind for it.

Fire becomes part of the crown's inner circle, and her judgement about who is loyal starts shaping how the coming war will be fought. She and Brigan move from hostility to a careful working trust and then to something more, complicated by his rank and by her certainty that she is a liability to anyone who loves her. Her long entanglement with Archer breaks down: he cannot stop being jealous, and one of Fire's own guards is carrying his child. The hardest thing she carries is what happened to Cansrel. He did not die by accident: Fire turned her father's own mind against him because she could see no other way to stop what he was doing to the kingdom, and living with that is what makes her so unwilling to use her power on anyone now. Meanwhile attempts are made on her life and on the royal family's, several by men whose minds have been tampered with, and the shape of the rebellion sharpens: Mydogg in the north, with Pikkian allies through his sister Murgda, and Gentian in the south, each preparing to move.

Fire is sent south into Lord Gentian's household as a spy, hiding what she is among his guests and using her power to map exactly who is committed to him and what he has promised them. The intelligence is what the crown needed: Gentian's part in the rising is dismantled and the southern half of the war collapses before it can properly begin. That leaves Mydogg in the north, better prepared, better allied and far more dangerous, and it leaves the unexplained mind-worker still unaccounted for. Archer, unable to sit still and increasingly obsessed with the fogged minds, goes north on his own to find whoever is responsible.

The second mind-worker turns out to be a boy with mismatched eyes and a compelling voice, the son of a man who came into the Dells from the unknown country beyond the western mountains. Whatever the boy says is believed and obeyed, and the people he has used are left blank afterwards. He kills Archer. Fire, in the north as the war closes in, is taken prisoner and held by Mydogg's people, and finds the boy there among her captors, fascinated by her and intent on keeping her. Her own power is what saves her: she can feel his working on her where nobody else can, and she can push back against it. Grieving, injured and alone, she gets herself free, while the two armies move toward the battle that will settle who rules the Dells.

The war ends in the north. Fire, who has spent the whole book refusing to use her power the way her father used his, finally uses it at his scale - across a battlefield, into thousands of minds at once - and uses it to stop men killing each other rather than to command them. The rising is broken and the crown holds. In the aftermath Fire learns that Brigan is not King Nax's son at all but Brocker's, which is why Nax had Brocker crippled, and which makes Brigan and the dead Archer half-brothers. Archer's child will be born into Brocker's household with Fire's support. Fire chooses to stay at the centre of the kingdom rather than hidden at its edge: she works for the crown, she is with Brigan without marrying into his family's throne, and she decides deliberately that there will be no more human monsters after her. The boy is never caught. He goes west through the mountains, into the country his father came from, carrying his voice with him.

characters.description: A publicly recognizable Galen's Institute cadet whose rapid advancement has earned him the unofficial title Iron Prince of Galen's. On his first date with Aria, he helps subdue four Penview cadets without seriously injuring them.
characters.name: Rei

characters.description: A leading first-year combatant at Galen's Institute and Rei's date. She works with him to restrain four Penview cadets who corner them at a mall, then shares the awkward discovery that their competitive fame now follows them off campus.
characters.name: Aria Laurent

characters.description: Rei's oldest friend and a skilled member of Aria's squad. She exploits the opening created by Rei's simulated shoulder sacrifice to eliminate the opposing Lancer during training. Her interest in Logan is already evident.
characters.name: Viviana Arada

characters.description: A powerful member of Aria's squad who reinforces Rei's group in training but resents accepting Rei's commands.
characters.name: Logan Grant

characters.description: A member of Aria's squad who is concerned that Rei's unexpected summons to the administration building may involve Shido.
characters.name: Layton Catchwick

characters.description: The Lancer in Aria's six-person squad. She fights beside Rei's group during sectional training when two opposing teams form an alliance against them.
characters.name: Chancery Cash

characters.description: Rei's anomalous CAD and the concealed reason his closest teammates suspect an administration summons may be dangerous. Its unusual development makes any official interest in Rei especially sensitive to him and his trusted friends.
characters.name: Shido

characters.description: Galen's chief combat instructor. She evaluates Aria's squad without favoritism, praises sound tactical choices, and corrects the command mistakes that accompany them. She expects cadets to understand both victory and its cost.
characters.name: Valera Dent

characters.description: Rei's brawler instructor. He summons Rei to the administration building after squad training, setting in motion a confidential meeting that Rei's friends fear may concern Shido and the limits placed around it.
characters.name: Michael Bretz

characters.description: Aria's uncle and the commanding officer of Galen's Institute. He personally oversees Kamiya Corporation's confidential sponsorship approach to Rei and warns that its interest appears disproportionate to Rei's public record.
characters.name: Rama Guest

characters.description: Kamiya Corporation's negotiator in its approach to Rei. She presents an extraordinary sponsorship package and admits the corporation has a private reason for moving before more established sponsors can approach him.
characters.name: Kamiya Corporation fixer

characters.description: The head of Kamiya Corporation and an A8 CAD user. He directs an aggressive effort to isolate Rei from competing sponsors, yet forbids pressure against Rei's friends or former home and shows a personal interest in Rei's abandonment.
characters.name: Dr. Kamiya Hiroto

characters.description: A Galen's medical officer who treats Rei after the manipulated fortitude test ruptures part of his lung. He joins the staff responsible for Rei's recovery, future examinations, and continuing medical checks.
characters.name: Willem Mayd

characters.description: A medical officer involved in Rei's recovery after his fortitude test is deliberately pushed beyond safe limits. She helps oversee his treatment and becomes part of Galen's expanded monitoring plan for his health.
characters.name: Amina Ashton

characters.description: The officer supervising Galen's elite squads during travel to Sectionals. He expects cadets to solve tactical problems independently and holds direct authority over Firesong throughout the tournament trip.
characters.name: Dyrk Reese

characters.description: An elite second-year Lancer traveling to Sectionals with Firesong. A former Sector 9 first-year champion, he is one of Galen's high-expectation competitors and a proven presence in the older-year bracket.
characters.name: Anatoly Sidorov

characters.description: A concealed participant in a plan to obtain covert access to an arena system. She arranges for a hidden, time-limited access tool to be delivered at the tournament through a contractor with a violent past.
characters.name: Solista Laurent

characters.description: An older Galen's competitor who previously trained Rei's group. At Sectionals, he publicly backs Rei and ends a rival cadet's attempt to provoke him before the tournament begins, acting as an experienced ally.
characters.name: Christopher Lennon

characters.description: An artificial intelligence with influence over SCT operations and a private communications link to Valera Dent. It concedes that Firesong's convenient opening pairing may have been arranged as a test for Rei.
characters.name: The Mind

characters.description: The officer who supervises Catcher's private test of Ruinous. She recognizes the ability's competitive potential and directs Firesong to practice silent mental activation so opponents cannot anticipate it.
characters.name: Sarah Takeshi

characters.description: Valormade's first-year Lancer leader and a leading Sectionals competitor. His Breakstep lets him control distance, and he defeats Viv before meeting Rei in the individual semifinal. He treats his defeated opponent responsibly.
characters.name: Castro Vadem

characters.description: Kenneth Academy's chief SCT arbiter. After the attack on Rei, she announces the arena-hack investigation, postpones affected competition, and suspends nonessential systems while software and physical security are reviewed.
characters.name: Major Ashling Jones

characters.description: Solista Laurent's adult son and Aria's brother, an S-ranked professional fighter concealed by a projection disguise. He destroys Solista's arena trigger and warns her that the real attack on Rei carries grave consequences.
characters.name: Aria's unnamed brother

characters.description: The ISCM officer assigned to monitor Rei for General Abel. She receives a priority notice that Shido has upgraded an existing unique ability and assigned another, continuing a formal reporting line focused on Rei.
characters.name: Cassidy Moran

characters.description: A Central Command authority who has assigned Cassidy Moran to monitor Rei and receive reports on Shido's unprecedented development. The reporting chain is alerted when Shido upgrades one unique ability and grants a second.
characters.name: General Abel

characters.description: A third-year Galen's cadet who joins another student in making Anatoly Sidorov leave Rei alone. She warns Rei that Sidorov is fixated on status and sees Rei's rise as a threat.
characters.name: Candace Meyer

characters.description: The birth identity behind Logan Grant. He begins disclosing this name to Firesong after apologizing to Rei, opening an account of the family history that shaped his hostility, secrecy, and reaction to perceived cowardice.
characters.name: Logan Galt

characters.description: Rei's specialist instructor after Sectionals. She works with Michael Bretz to train Rei across Shido's three modes and improve his control of Temporal Step, including the ability's demanding repeated use.
characters.name: Katori Amala

characters.description: Firesong's Saber sub-instructor. She leads additional team training while Rei receives separate instruction in Shido's modes and Temporal Step. Her work focuses on the five other members' coordination and tactical weaknesses.
characters.name: Claire DeSoto

characters.description: Aria's father, a Rook-class frontline general and former Galen's cadet. He arrives without warning to argue that Galen's and Firesong may be limiting Aria's development despite her rank and the team's recent success.
characters.name: General Carmen Laurent

characters.description: A male Laurent relative and Sergeant Major recruited by Kamiya Corporation for work involving his younger sister's training. He accepts the assignment as the corporation begins assembling support for Firesong.
characters.name: Unnamed Laurent Sergeant Major

recaps.ending: Firesong leaves Sectionals as the first-year team-battle champion, although Rei's injuries forced the other five members to win the final without him. Rei and Aria's hacked individual final is recorded as a draw. Rei recovers into specialized training at C9 with Shido's Brawler, Saber, and Phalanx modes, Type Shift 2, and the short-range jump ability Temporal Step. His fibrodysplasia shows no new flare-ups and may be in remission, but medical monitoring continues. Logan reconciles with Rei, tells Firesong the history behind his former identity, and joins Chancery in learning Shido's S-ranked Growth secret. Rei and Aria remain together, while Viv continues to fear that her development is falling behind the team. Central's coerced transfer threat leaves Rei, Aria, and Firesong with demanding Systems and InterSystems targets if they are to stay at Galen's Institute. Carmen refuses to sign voluntarily, and Galen's promises greater support. Rei reopens negotiations with Kamiya only for team sponsorship, rejects personal payment, and learns that the corporation's head initiated the offer. Kamiya accepts the team condition in principle. Rei has not reconciled with Hiroto or Sarah, while Solista's opposition, the unidentified arena attacker, and Shido's limits all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Rei and Aria begin dating as Firesong prepares for Sectionals, while Kamiya Corporation offers Rei a suspiciously generous sponsorship tied to the family that abandoned him. Central manipulates Rei's fortitude test, and Shido continues evolving at an extraordinary pace. At Sectionals, Firesong advances despite targeted brackets and internal strain. Catcher gains Ruinous, Chancery gains Warband, and the team suspects Shido may affect nearby CADs. Rei reaches the individual final against Aria, but an arena hack subjects him to S0 projections and leaves him badly injured. Shido rises to C9, adds a Phalanx mode, and grants the short-range jump ability Temporal Step. Firesong wins the team-battle championship without Rei, while the interrupted duel is declared a draw. Logan reveals his former identity and reconciles with the team. Central then uses a transfer order to demand exceptional Systems and InterSystems results from Rei, Aria, and Firesong. Rei seeks Kamiya sponsorship for the whole team instead of himself, and Kamiya agrees in principle, while its head is revealed as Rei's estranged grandfather.

recaps.text: Previously: Rei entered Galen's Institute with Shido, a CAD whose S-ranked Growth made his development both exceptional and dangerous to reveal. Viviana Arada remained his oldest friend, while Aria Laurent became the commander of the six-person squad that also included Catcher, Chancery Cash, and Logan Grant. Rei's rise brought growing attention from Galen's staff, the ISCM, and other cadets. His relationships within the squad were uneven: Aria and Catcher were trusted allies, Viv was fiercely protective of him, and Logan's hostility remained a threat to the group's cohesion. As the new term begins, Rei and Aria are prominent first-year fighters, their squad is preparing for higher competition, and the secret of Shido's growth still shapes who Rei can trust.

Rei and Aria's first date ends in an off-campus fight when four Penview cadets corner them. Security footage clears the pair, but an autograph request shows that their Galen's reputation has become public. Back at the Institute, Aria's squad defeats two allied training teams, with Rei taking temporary command and sacrificing a simulated shoulder so Viv can strike decisively. Logan still resents following Rei, though Viv confronts him and makes any future relationship conditional on changing his conduct. Rei is then summoned to a confidential meeting with Galen's commanding officer and a Kamiya Corporation representative. Kamiya offers a remarkably rich sponsorship despite Rei's limited public record. Rei refuses to sign immediately, suspecting the corporation knows something about him or Shido. Kamiya's head, Dr. Kamiya Hiroto, responds by planning to block rival sponsors and shows an unexplained personal concern with Rei's abandonment and medical history. Rei links Kamiya to his biological family and shares the suspicion with Viv. The resulting distress disrupts squad training, while Logan begins apologizing and Rei prepares to trust Aria and Catcher with more of the truth.

Rei tells Aria and Catcher that Kamiya's offer may come from the family that abandoned him. Independent reviewers find the contract genuine and unusually favorable, leaving its motive as the central concern. Rei also concludes that Shido may need varied, stronger opponents to maintain its rapid gains. Logan distances himself from former associates and starts making tentative efforts to join the group. During parameter testing, Rei openly compares Shido's Brawler and Saber modes, but the final fortitude trial is secretly altered. He collapses with a lung injury after reaching conditions later measured at A1. Galen's officers determine that the manipulation points to Central Command, which appears to be probing Rei as a strategically important user. Rei receives treatment from Willem Mayd and Amina Ashton, then returns under strict medical and training controls. Chancery presses him to explain Shido, and Logan privately infers that its Growth is the key, but Rei does not confirm the secret. After recovering enough to travel, Aria's six-person squad departs for Sector 9 Sectionals under Dyrk Reese. The team receives its official competitive name: Firesong.

While Firesong arrives at Sectionals, Solista Laurent participates in a covert plan to obtain arena-system access. Christopher Lennon ends a public provocation against Rei, and Logan gives Rei a direct apology without yet explaining the trauma behind his anger. All six members qualify. Firesong wins its opening team battle by hiding CAD light in a blizzard and ambushing its opponents. Reese tries to punish the team for prolonging Rei's final confrontation, but Valera Dent accepts their tactical explanation. The Mind privately admits it may have arranged the pairing to test Rei. Shido gains unexpected improvements, while Viv and Logan's relationship becomes public. Firesong survives a war game, and Catcher defeats a stronger Phalanx despite a broken shoulder. His CAD evolves and grants Ruinous, a repeatable charged burst powerful enough to bend Aria's shield. In a later zero-gravity war game, three teams target Firesong. The squad reunites after being separated, Catcher deploys Ruinous, and Firesong wins the quarterfinal. Immediately afterward, Chancery receives an undisclosed CAD notification that leaves her shocked.

Chancery's new ability, Warband, creates three overlapping spear attacks and defeats Aria in testing. Coming so soon after Ruinous, it raises the possibility that prolonged proximity to Shido is affecting other CADs. Viv, the only Firesong member without an ability, fears that the team will outgrow her. She performs strongly in team competition but abandons a useful stealth advantage in an individual quarterfinal against Castro Vadem and loses. Her CAD ranks up without granting an ability, deepening that fear. Firesong is then overwhelmed in a Wargame semifinal after the other teams coordinate against it. Solista, watching in disguise, is revealed as Aria's mother and decides that Rei and Firesong threaten Aria's future. Firesong later defeats Red Crown and advances to the team-battle final against Valormade. Rei beats Vadem to reach the individual final, while Aria defeats Logan to become his opponent. Before those matches, Aria helps Rei confront his tendency to blame himself for the team's difficulties. They kiss and agree that they are now in a relationship.

Rei gains the advantage over Aria in the first-year final, but the arena freezes the match and spawns six S0 sparring projections that repeatedly attack him. Valera Dent breaches the field boundary and forces a reset, ending the assault. Investigators identify an arena back door installed days earlier, but not the attacker. Solista had separately brought a trigger intended to hinder Aria's opponent. Her adult son, Aria's brother, destroys it after she denies activating it. Shido's response to the attack raises Rei from C7 to C9, upgrades Type Shift, adds a heavily armored Phalanx mode, and assigns Temporal Step. Rei and Aria re-enter a practice field under supervision despite their trauma. Temporal Step moves Rei across a short distance by a jump-like mechanism rather than ordinary speed, but it causes fleeting visions and severe nausea. Reese reacts to its implications with threatening language and is removed as chaperone. Rei's extensive injuries keep him out of the team final. Firesong agrees to compete with five members. The Mind cannot trace the hack, suspects a rogue actor within the hierarchy rather than Central as a whole, and adds monitoring to every arena Rei uses.

Anatoly Sidorov confronts the injured Rei over Shido until older Galen's cadets intervene. Firesong enters the team-battle final one member short. Aria struggles at the boundary where the attack occurred, but Viv helps her enter. The team draws Valormade into an encirclement, then converges on Castro Vadem and commits Ruinous, Warband, and Overclock at once. Firesong wins the first-year team-battle championship without Rei. Officials record Rei and Aria's interrupted individual final as a draw. Afterward, Rei decides that Logan and Chancery have earned the right to know Shido's secret. Logan first reveals that he was born Logan Galt. He explains how his father's abandonment of a threatened civilian sector led to mass death, disgrace, and the destruction of his family. His mother changed the children's identities and later died, while Logan was separated from his sister. Firesong accepts him, and Rei recognizes how their different traumas fueled their conflict. Rei then shows Logan and Chancery Shido's S-ranked Growth and unique abilities. The team leaves Sectionals more cohesive. Kamiya accelerates its effort to secure Rei and tells Sarah Takeshi that Rei is her younger brother. Reese is removed from Galen's after his campaign against Rei exceeds the authority Central granted him.

Back at Galen's, Rei trains Shido's Brawler, Saber, and Phalanx modes with Michael Bretz and Katori Amala while Claire DeSoto develops the rest of Firesong. Temporal Step becomes more controllable, though nausea still limits repeated use. Medical checks find no new fibrodysplasia flare-ups and suggest Rei may be in remission. Aria's father, General Carmen Laurent, then arrives with a transfer order. He argues that Galen's and Firesong limit Aria, but both she and Rei refuse to leave. Rei identifies the order as a Central pressure tactic that makes Carmen the required signatory. Carmen will not sign voluntarily, yet warns that Central can compel him. He gives Galen's a chance to prevent the transfer: Rei and Aria must win at Systems, Firesong must win team battle and War Games, and they must reach InterSystems. Galen's promises intensified support. Rei decides additional resources are necessary and reopens talks with Kamiya. He will consider sponsorship only if the corporation identifies who initiated the offer, supports all of Firesong, and pays him nothing personally. Kamiya accepts the team condition in principle and begins recruiting staff. Its head, Hiroto, is revealed as Rei's estranged grandfather. The family conflict, Central's coercion, and the identity of the arena attacker remain open.

characters.description: Now an experienced member of the Reckoners and the man publicly credited with killing Steelheart. He still keeps notebooks on Epics and their weaknesses, and he has begun to think about a question the rest of the team considers dangerous: whether the corruption that turns Epics cruel is caused by the power itself or by something that can be resisted. He is a competent operative, an unreliable metaphorist, and privately determined to find Megan again.
characters.name: David Charleston

characters.description: The founder and leader of the Reckoners: a former schoolteacher, meticulous planner, and secretly an Epic himself, whose forcefields, healing and matter-manipulation are lent to his team through equipment rather than used openly. He restricts his own use of them because using an Epic's power drags its holder toward cruelty. Only David and Tia know what he is.
characters.name: Prof

characters.description: The Reckoners' intelligence specialist and the person who has known Prof longest. She keeps the team's records, watches Prof's use of his abilities more closely than he likes, and is the closest thing the organisation has to a conscience about its own leader.
characters.name: Tia

characters.description: A young woman David served with in Newcago, and an Epic whose ability returns her to life after she is killed. She left the Reckoners after Steelheart's fall rather than stay with a team whose purpose is killing people like her. David believes she resisted the corruption that comes with using Epic powers, and finding her again is his private reason for taking this assignment.
characters.name: Megan

characters.description: An Epic who moves and fights as living electricity, one of a series that has been attacking Newcago since Steelheart's death. Stopping her requires the Reckoners to work out what cancels her invulnerability before she can do serious damage to the city.
characters.name: Sourcefield

characters.description: The High Epic who rules Babilar, the flooded ruin of Manhattan. She raised the sea over the city and can appear as a projection of herself anywhere there is standing water, seeing and speaking through it, which makes privacy in her city effectively impossible. She is among the oldest and most calculating of the High Epics.
characters.name: Regalia

characters.description: The leader of the Reckoner cell operating in Babilar: guarded, territorial, and unimpressed by the arrival of a team from Newcago with a reputation and a plan of its own.
characters.name: Val

characters.description: A large, genial member of the Babilar cell with an entirely professional interest in corpses and an unshakeable good humour about the work.
characters.name: Exel

characters.description: The youngest member of the Babilar cell, a fast-talking demolitions specialist who is delighted to have new people to talk to and adapts to the incoming team faster than her colleagues do.
characters.name: Mizzy

characters.description: A member of the Babilar Reckoner cell, part of the local team the Newcago group is folded into on arrival.
characters.name: Sam

characters.description: An Epic who accumulates heat and releases it, capable of destroying an entire city and known to have done so, and who regards the destruction as a judgement he has been appointed to carry out. He can move himself instantly from place to place, which makes him nearly impossible to corner.
characters.name: Obliteration

characters.description: An Epic who returns any force used against her back onto whoever used it, which makes conventional attacks not merely useless but suicidal. She runs a gang in Babilar and serves Regalia's interests.
characters.name: Newton

characters.description: The hidden Epic responsible for the fruit that grows on Babilar's buildings and glows at night, and for the luminous images that appear on its walls. The city has been quietly fed and lit by this power for years without knowing where it came from.
characters.name: Dawnslight

recaps.ending: Regalia gets exactly what she was working toward and then dies. Her design was never to kill the Reckoners: she was dying, and she wanted a successor, so she engineered a situation in which Prof had to use his powers at full strength under extreme emotional pressure in order to save David from drowning. He does, and he gives in to the corruption that comes with them. Obliteration's attempt to destroy Babilar with the heat he has spent the book gathering is stopped and the city survives, but he escapes rather than dying. Megan, who has learned to use her ability by confronting what frightens her instead of avoiding it, is fully back on David's side, and their relationship is settled. Prof, now a fallen Epic and one of the most powerful alive, turns on the Reckoners and breaks with them, leaving the organisation shattered and David, Megan, Tia and Mizzy holding what is left of it. David refuses to accept that Prof is beyond recovery: Megan is his proof that an Epic can face the fear the power feeds on and come back from it, and the next book's objective is to do the same for Prof rather than to kill him.
recaps.in_short: With Steelheart dead, Epics keep arriving in Newcago to test the Reckoners, and the team works out that they are being sent by Regalia, a High Epic ruling the flooded ruin of Manhattan, now called Babilar. Prof takes David and Tia east to deal with her. Babilar is a drowned city of glowing fruit and fatalistic people, run by an Epic who can appear through any standing water, and David soon finds Megan there working for her. While the team hunts Regalia's lieutenants and the city-destroying Epic Obliteration prepares to incinerate Babilar, David works out that Megan's power is broader than resurrection and that an Epic who faces their deepest fear can use their abilities without being corrupted. Regalia's real plan proves to be her own succession: she is dying, and she manoeuvres Prof into using his powers under desperate emotional pressure so that he will fall. He does. Regalia dies, Babilar is saved, Obliteration escapes, and Prof turns on the Reckoners, leaving David determined to redeem him rather than kill him.

recaps.text: Previously: about a decade ago a red star called Calamity appeared in the sky and ordinary people began gaining superhuman powers. Almost every one of them used those powers to rule or destroy, and they became known as Epics. Chicago became Newcago, a steel city held under permanent artificial night by the High Epic Steelheart. David Charleston, whose father Steelheart killed in front of him, joined the Reckoners, the only organisation that assassinates Epics, and helped them kill Steelheart by working out that he could not be harmed by anyone who did not fear him. In the process David learned two secrets. The Reckoners' leader, Prof, is himself an Epic, whose forcefield, healing and matter-manipulation powers are lent to the team through equipment, and who avoids using them because Epic powers corrupt whoever uses them.
